output.brief: Please hold the breach notice. The rise in Corvane's missed bags is not explained by the new handler. Pelion uses the same Tessaly crews and its rate did not change. The extra missed bags are almost all bags diverted to the manual encode desk. Daily diversions went from about 70 to about 460, and about 91% of the missed bags reached the lateral after it closed. The diversions follow Corvane's tag stock. Tags printed on Fennick stock since 1 Sep fail automatic reading at about 11.8%, against about 1.5% on the old Brackwater stock. Pelion tags and transfer tags read normally. On 14–16 Oct, counters that used Brackwater stock from stores read at 1.6%, while kiosks on Fennick stock in the same days failed at 12.1%. The reader equipment looks fine. What is still unknown is whether the Fennick media itself is faulty or the printer heat settings need adjusting for it. Both fit the data, and kiosk cleaning also became less frequent. Next steps: return counters and kiosks to Brackwater stock now. About five weeks are in stores and the contract is valid to 31 Dec. Then test Fennick with the printer manufacturer's settings before any claim against Fennick. If the diversion rate falls, you have your answer. Revisit Tessaly's staffing separately.
